neighbours.label: The comma that closes an inserted attribution or aside (', says the mayor,' / ', she recalled,') where the interrupted main clause resumes, vs list commas and unbroken clauses
fire: The real problem, says the mayor, is the lack of cheap housing.
The first winter, she recalled, was the hardest of her life.
Most of the damage, according to the report, came from the flood.
That decision, the coach admits, cost them the title.
The best time to visit, locals say, is early October.
His first car, he remembered, had no heater at all.
The new policy, critics argue, will hurt small farms.
The old station, officials said, will reopen next year.
quiet: The real problem is the lack of cheap housing, says the mayor.
The first winter was the hardest of her life.
Most of the damage came from the flood in March.
That decision cost them the title last year.
We packed bread, cheese, apples and water for the trip.
His first car was red, small and very loud.
Critics argue that the new policy will hurt small farms.
Officials said that the old station will reopen next year.

predictions: The closing comma of a mid-sentence attribution reaches 0.2-0.5; list commas and attribution at the end of the sentence stay under 0.1.
notes: Probe: ', says the professor,' 0.463, 'have shown that' 0.327, ', he remembered,' 0.199, 'If all goes to plan,' 0.178; list commas 0.014-0.021. Only the reporting-verb aside was strong, so fire items all use one; amplitude may be weak.
